Most smart home lighting solutions rely on small bulbs and plug-in adapters, but as the market matures, we are starting to see recessed ceiling lights with built-in Matter support and direct compatibility with Apple Home. SwitchBot has just launched the all-new SwitchBot RGBICWW ceiling light, which natively supports Matter, requires no additional setup, and delivers very high brightness output.

HomeKit Weekly is a series dedicated to introducing smart home accessories, automation tips, and all information related to the Apple smart home framework.

Native Matter and Apple Home integration

The biggest selling point of this new ceiling light is that it requires no SwitchBot Hub at all and supports Matter right out of the box. As long as the Apple TV 4K or HomePod at home stays connected, the fixture can join your existing smart home system directly over the 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network.

Size and brightness specifications

SwitchBot offers two sizes to suit different scenarios: the 12-inch model is ideal for hallways and bathrooms, providing 2,000 lumens of brightness; the larger 15-inch model is suitable for living rooms and bedrooms, with a maximum brightness of up to 3,200 lumens. It also supports stepless dimming, allowing smooth adjustment from 100% all the way down to 0%.

Most standard smart bulbs can typically only display one colour at a time, but this fixture uses RGBIC technology, which uses independent chips to present multiple colours on the ceiling simultaneously, creating richly varied lighting effects. If you prefer more traditional lighting, it is also equipped with dedicated warm-white and cool-white LEDs, with colour temperature adjustable from 2700K to 6500K. In addition, it has a power-off memory function—even during a brief power outage, the fixture will retain the brightness and colour settings you previously configured. Summary: SwitchBot RGBICWW

Using 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi means you will need to keep an extra device running on the traditional frequency band on your router. In my view, if it could have a built-in Thread radio and support mesh networking to achieve near-instantaneous response times, the user experience would be even better. Being able to buy a wired-installed, natively Matter-supported ceiling light for under US$50 is absolutely an extremely cost-effective choice for anyone looking to permanently upgrade their ceiling lighting.

You can head over to Amazon right now to buy this brand-new SwitchBot RGBICWW.
